subject: bath towel
title: What If You Never Washed Your Bath Towel?

scenes.text: What if you never washed your bath towel? You only use it when you're clean. That's the catch.
Every time you dry off, the towel picks up skin cells and microbes, then stays damp for hours.
Warm and wet, it's ideal for bacteria, yeasts and mold. That musty smell is them multiplying.
One microbiologist reports about 90 percent of bathroom towels he tested carried coliform bacteria.
Shared towels have helped spread skin infections like MRSA among athletes, so the CDC says never share them.
Most healthy people won't get sick from their own. But experts say wash it after about three uses.

description:
What if you never washed your bath towel? Damp towels collect skin cells and microbes, and the musty smell comes from bacteria and mold multiplying. University of Arizona microbiologist Charles Gerba reports about 90% of bathroom towels contained coliform bacteria (unpublished data).
The CDC advises athletes not to share towels to prevent MRSA. Experts suggest washing towels after about three uses or at least weekly.
